title: [Decision] The merge queue merged a group whose full-suite `CI` run concluded FAILURE — measured on `77da09bac`, now on main
body:
Filed by the `pm-dispatch` seat. ⚠️ **This is a protection-mechanism finding, not a test failure.** It concerns repository/queue configuration, which is a maintainer surface, so it is a decision card rather than a work card.

⚠️ **Disclosure first: my own two PRs are the ones that went through the hole.** #9270 and #9274 are this seat's dispatches; I flipped and enqueued both. Their artifacts verify clean on main and the failing test is unrelated to either diff, so the *outcome* looks benign — but the *mechanism* that let them land would equally let a real regression land, which is why this is filed rather than quietly noted.

## The measurement

Merge-queue branch `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-9270-5d4f3d5d8221a3133088e5a0eb4fa90df5749294`, queue head **`77da09bac`**. Five workflow runs, one attempt each, read individually:

| conclusion | workflow |
|---|---|
| success | ADR Merge Approval |
| success | Spec Liveness Check |
| success | Console Pin Freshness |
| success | Lint & Type Check |
| **failure** | **CI** (run [32017635668](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32017635668)) |

The failing job is `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, step *"Run driver-sql suite against both live servers"*, failing test:

```
FAIL src/sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts
  > os migrate plan lists the MySQL widening (#3954)
  > applies exactly what it planned, and then finds nothing l…
```

Timeline: the `CI` run concluded `failure` at **10:10:24Z**. #9270 and #9274 both reported `merged` at **10:10:45Z** — 21 seconds later. There was **no second attempt** (`run_attempt=1` on all five runs) and no re-queue.

And the decisive check, run locally against a fresh `git fetch origin main`:

```
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 77da09bac origin/main && echo YES
YES — the commit whose CI run FAILED is on main
```

`origin/main` now reads `6a1b45ec2` (#9274) on top of `77da09bac` (#9270).

## Why this matters more than the failing test

The repo's stated model is that the queue runs the **full** suite precisely because PR-side CI runs only the affected subset — the `merge-queue-triage` workflow (#4859) says so in its own comment on this very build:

> 队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里

That bot then posted a careful three-branch triage checklist whose whole premise is that a red queue build **blocks**, and the operator must decide whether to re-queue. Twenty-one seconds later the group merged anyway. So the triage workflow is advising on a decision that is not actually being enforced, and a reviewer reading that comment would reasonably conclude the merge was held.

⭐ **This is the seventh instance this shift of a derived or declared safeguard consumed as authoritative while not doing what it claims** — #9171 (`dispatch-gates.mjs` omits gates CI runs), #9182 (os-regen driver drops a side at exit 0), #9192 (docs-drift listed by package dependency), the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` gate being structurally blind to the `Fixes` direction, #8990's census (a key-shaped grep measured 12 where there were 57), #9282 (docs-drift has "no opinion" on the file carrying a rule three pages restate), and this. The difference is that this one is the *last* line of defence rather than an advisory.

## What I could NOT determine, and will not guess

⛔ **I cannot read branch-protection / merge-queue required-check configuration with the tools available to this seat.** So I can state that a red `CI` run did not block, but **not why**. The two candidate mechanisms, neither verified:

1. **`CI` is not in the queue's required-checks set** — only `Lint & Type Check` / `Spec Liveness Check` / `Console Pin Freshness` / `ADR Merge Approval` are. Then the full suite is observational, and the #4859 triage bot is documenting a gate that does not exist.
2. **A name-matching failure** — the required check is registered under a name that no longer matches the emitted job/check-run name, so it is treated as "not reported" rather than "failed", and something is configured to merge anyway.

These have different fixes and the difference is not cosmetic, so this needs someone who can read the settings.

## The decision

- **A — the full suite SHOULD block** (my read of the stated intent): add `CI` to the queue's required checks, or repair the name match. Then re-triage the failing test below on its own merits.
- **B — the full suite is deliberately observational**, and the queue gates only on the fast checks. Then #4859's triage comment is misleading and should say so out loud, and the "队列跑的是全量套件" framing needs rewriting — because right now it reads as a guarantee.
- **C — something else** in the configuration that I cannot see.

## Secondary, and separable

`sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts > os migrate plan lists the MySQL widening (#3954)` failed on a queue build whose only PR-side content was a **JSDoc comment change** (#9270 touches one file, comment-only) plus #9274. It cannot have been caused by #9270. Two live candidates, ⛔ neither measured:

- genuinely flaky against the live MySQL service (the triage bot reported *"过去 24h 队列共有 1 个失败构建（不含本次）"* — a second data point exists);
- **or** interference from #9274's new `sql-driver-diagnostic-value-probe.test.ts`, which creates tables (`probe_9160_mysql`) and raises errors against the *same* live MySQL server in the same suite. I flagged this as the first hypothesis to test rather than reaching for "flaky" — but note #9274's own PR-side `Temporal Conformance` job was **green**, which is evidence against it.

Whichever it is, it merged to main red, so `main` may currently be red on that test.

## Related

#4859 (the merge-queue triage workflow) · #9182 (the generated-docs serialization point, why these PRs are in the queue repeatedly) · #9171, #9192, #9282 (the same "safeguard is narrower than it claims" family) · PR #9270, PR #9274 (this seat's, the two that landed) · #3954 (the failing test's origin card)
